record.paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures on Submanifolds of Finite Type: Recent Development
record.original_question: Is every compact surface in E³ whose position vector field admits a finite spectral decomposition into Laplace eigenmaps necessarily an ordinary sphere?

evidence.quote: The immersion x is said to be of finite type if the position vector field of M in E^m... can be expressed as a finite sum of E^m-valued eigenfunctions of the Laplace operator.
Conjecture 1. The only compact surfaces of finite type in E^3 are the ordinary spheres.
However, after more than two decades Conjecture 1 remains open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E^3$ denote 3-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard inner product, and let $M \subset E^3$ be a smooth compact surface isometrically immersed in $E^3$ via $x: M \to E^3$. Let $\Delta$ denote the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the induced Riemannian metric on $M$, acting componentwise on $E^3$-valued smooth functions. The immersion $x$ is said to be of finite type if the position vector field admits a finite decomposition
$$x = x_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{k} x_i,$$
where $x_0 \in E^3$ is a constant vector and each $x_i: M \to E^3$ is a non-constant smooth map satisfying $\Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i$ for some real number $\lambda_i$, with $k$ finite.

Prove or disprove: every compact surface of finite type in $E^3$ is an ordinary round sphere.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that the only compact finite-type surfaces in $E^3$ are ordinary spheres, posed by B.-Y. Chen in the 1980s, remains an active and open problem. Recent works (e.g., on finite Chen-type surfaces, Gauss maps, and various special classes) continue to investigate special cases, with spheres still being the only known compact examples, but no general proof or counterexample has appeared.

status_evidence.title: On Surfaces of finite Chen-type
status_evidence.snippet: Studies finite Chen-type surfaces; spheres remain the only known compact examples.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of compact finite-type surfaces in E^3 is still being investigated, with spheres as the only known examples.

status_evidence.title: Quadrics with finite Chen-type Gauss map
status_evidence.snippet: Up to this moment the only known finite Chen-type surfaces in E^3 are portions of spheres, circular cylinders and minimal surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Among compact such surfaces, only spheres are known, and the general conjecture remains open.
